extracted.intended_audience: early-career researchers applying to the DOE Office of Science Early Career Research Program
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting an application (pre-application then full application if encouraged) to the DOE Office of Science Early Career Research Program, meeting eligibility, topical, and merit-review criteria. Focus is on basic research within Office of Science program areas and demonstrating investigator potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program funding duration and amount
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding is for at least five years at $750,000+ per year for university-based researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program provides multi-year, substantial support intended to enable formative early-career research; applicants should plan proposals consistent with long-term funding and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — Career stage (time since Ph.D.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 10 years of receiving a Ph.D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must meet the post-Ph.D. time-window requirement at the time of application; exceptions or extensions are not described here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — Appointment/employer
rubrics_metrics.description: Untenured Assistant or Associate Professor at U.S. academic institution OR full-time employee at DOE National Laboratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must hold one of the listed positions/appointments to be eligible; visiting/adjunct or non-U.S. institution appointments are not listed as eligible here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — Citizenship/residency
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. or foreign national in the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants need not be U.S. citizens but must be physically in the U.S.; confirm any additional security or access requirements with program guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review mechanism — competitive peer review by outside experts
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding competitively awarded on the basis of peer review. Selection based on peer review by outside scientific experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals are evaluated by external scientific peers; applicants should write for knowledgeable technical reviewers and ensure clarity of significance, approach, and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission process — two-stage pre-application requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-stage process: pre-applications reviewed first. Only applicants whose pre-application is encouraged may submit full applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must submit a pre-application and be explicitly encouraged to proceed to full submission; invest effort in a strong pre-application to secure invitation to the full stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research topic fit — programmatic priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed research topics must fall within the programmatic priorities of DOE's Office of Science (programs include ASCR, BES, BER, FES, HEP, NP, Isotope R&D and Production, Accelerator R&D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the proposed work maps clearly to one of the listed Office of Science program areas and articulates relevance to that program's priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research focus — support for basic research (not commercial/customer-driven)
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeks to support BASIC research to advance understanding rather than to address commercial opportunities. Applications proposing research related to current commercial activity or current customer needs may be declined without merit review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should emphasize fundamental scientific questions and advances in understanding rather than immediate commercial applications or customer-driven product development; proposals that appear commercial may be screened out prior to review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation — scientific and/or technical merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific and/or technical merit of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will assess the importance, rigor, and potential impact of the scientific/technical ideas and objectives articulated in the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation — appropriateness of proposed method or approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriateness of the proposed method or approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the proposed experimental/theoretical/computational approaches are well-suited to the objectives, including study design, methodology, and feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation — competency of personnel and adequacy of resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Competency of personnel and adequacy of proposed resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate whether the PI and team have the qualifications, complementary expertise, and institutional support (equipment, facilities) necessary to execute the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation — reasonableness and appropriateness of the proposed budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasonableness and appropriateness of the proposed budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget must be realistic, justified, and aligned with proposed activities; reviewers consider whether costs are necessary and appropriate for achieving the objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation — relevance and importance to mission needs and program priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevance and importance to mission needs and program priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should clearly articulate how the research advances DOE mission areas and aligns with the specific priorities of the selected Office of Science program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation — likelihood of success and investigator development
rubrics_metrics.description: Likelihood of success and development of the early-career investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess both feasibility of achieving project aims and the project's potential to foster the applicant's growth as an independent researcher (career development impact).
